findings.title: REQ-DLV-002's procedure says every agent definition states that an engineering agent cannot grant a real business, Finance or IT approval, but no definition in .claude/agents states it directly
findings.reproduction: In a fresh clone at e11b5f08dfa8b6cbe8716964e3412e17697234aa, the REQ-DLV-002 procedure in docs/delivery/requirements.csv reads: 'project rules and every agent definition state that an engineering agent cannot grant a real business, Finance or IT approval'. Running grep -l -i -E 'never grants?|cannot grant|can never grant|no agent grants' .claude/agents/*.md matches none of the ten definitions. backend-workflow-engineer.md line 26 comes closest: business approvals are human actions and timers never approve. Every definition instead ends with 'Read docs/delivery/agent-protocol.md and CLAUDE.md before you start any assignment', and both of those files state the rule (CLAUDE.md line 13; agent-protocol.md lines 9-10).
findings.expected: Either each agent definition carries the one-line rule that an engineering agent never grants a real business, Finance or IT approval (and that product G6 never implies DG7), or the REQ-DLV-002 procedure says the definitions incorporate the rule through the mandatory reading of CLAUDE.md and agent-protocol.md.
findings.actual: The rule applies to every agent in substance, because each definition makes reading CLAUDE.md and agent-protocol.md mandatory, and REQ-DLV-002's acceptance criterion names only those two files. Only the register's procedure wording overstates where the rule is written. This is a wording inconsistency with no behavioural effect, and I would accept it as an observation.

history.note: Reported in the DG0 round-7 domain review. Wording only; I would accept it as an observation (Low, non-mandatory).
